Accessibility is the ability of a website to be consulted by all types of users.

The concept of accessibility was first used for people with disabilities (visually impaired, blind...). Indeed, the latter use specific tools to navigate the web (screen readers software, Braille ranges...), and only compliance with the WCAG (Web Content Accessibility Guidelines) standards defined by the WAI (Web Accessibility Initiative) allows a website to be read by such tools.

In fact, accessibility is for all of us, because the conditions for consulting a website can vary according to the tools, the location, the climatic conditions, and many other things. For example, a user operating a tablet or smartphone in direct sunlight will not have the same reading and navigation conditions as a user behind a desktop computer without high brightness or noise.
